usage: agentbreeder new agent [-h]
                              [--model {anthropic,gemini,ollama,openai,openrouter,vertex}]
                              [--vertex-project PROJECT]
                              [--vertex-location LOCATION] [--model-id ID]
                              [--runtime REF] [--dir DIR |
                              --stack-for AGENT_YAML] [--from-spec FILE]
                              [--dry-run] [--expect-digest SHA256] [--json]
                              name

Write a starter agent project to DIR (default ./NAME): agent.yaml, stack.yaml
(Postgres and LiteLLM), stack/litellm/config.yaml, and editable sources in
src/prompt/ and src/evals/. Publishes prompt/NAME-prompt@0.1.0 and eval/NAME-
evals@0.1.0 into DIR/registry and writes agent.lock. DIR must not exist or be
an empty directory.

positional arguments:
  name                  Agent name: [a-z][a-z0-9-], at most 31 characters

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --model {anthropic,gemini,ollama,openai,openrouter,vertex}
                        Model provider, called through LiteLLM (required,
                        except with --from-spec); gemini, openai and
                        openrouter have been run end to end with their default
                        models, anthropic and vertex are config-only; vertex
                        makes the plain starter only, not --stack-for or
                        --from-spec
  --vertex-project PROJECT
                        With --model vertex: the Google Cloud project id of
                        the service-account key
  --vertex-location LOCATION
                        With --model vertex: the Vertex AI location, e.g. us-
                        central1 or global
  --model-id ID         LiteLLM model id, PROVIDER/... (default: the
                        provider's own, e.g.
                        openrouter/google/gemini-3.8-flash; openrouter ids are
                        openrouter/<vendor>/<model>)
  --runtime REF         Runtime version agent.yaml pins, runtime/NAME@X.Y.Z
                        (default: runtime/adk@1.4.0, the only one the starter
                        has been run end to end on); `agentbreeder registry
                        runtimes` lists them
  --dir DIR             Destination (default ./NAME)
  --stack-for AGENT_YAML
                        Instead of a starter, write stack.yaml and
                        stack/litellm/config.yaml beside an existing
                        agent.yaml named NAME (onboarding an agent.yaml alone)
  --from-spec FILE      Write the project from an agent-builder spec: a
                        private JSON file (mode 0600) with the model, prompt
                        text, eval cases, tools and MCP servers
                        (docs/commands/new.md)
  --dry-run             Show what would be written
  --expect-digest SHA256
                        With --stack-for: refuse unless agent.yaml still has
                        this digest (agent_sha256 from --dry-run --json); with
                        --from-spec: unless the plan is the previewed one
                        (plan_sha256)
  --json                Print the result as JSON
